content: 1. Exercise caution and monitor when co-administering drugs metabolized predominantly by CYP3A, as dose adjustments may be necessary. Crizotinib increases erythromycin stearate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 2. ECG monitoring is recommended when using drugs that may prolong the QT interval. Crofelemer increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Crofelemer may also inhibit MRP2 and OATP1A2 transporters in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases cyclosporine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, while cyclosporine increases erythromycin stearate levels through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin stearate increases dabigatran levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if creatinine clearance (CrCl) is <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 5. Dabrafenib decreases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 6. Erythromycin stearate increases dactinomycin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 7. Danicopan increases erythromycin stearate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where small concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases dapsone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases daridorexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit daridorexant dose to 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 11. Both dasatinib and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases daunorubicin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Deferasirox decreases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases deflazacort levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 15. Both deutetrabenazine and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. Deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent at the maximum recommended dose. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases dexamethasone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 17. Erythromycin stearate increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. 18. Erythromycin stearate decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases their levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases digoxin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Erythromycin stearate increases docetaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 22. Both dolasetron and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 23. Erythromycin stearate increases donepezil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases doxorubicin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 25. Erythromycin stearate increases dutasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Duvelisib increases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin stearate increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Elagolix increases erythromycin stearate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 29. Eliglustat decreases erythromycin stearate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 30. Eluxadoline increases erythromycin stearate levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 32. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant concentrations, increasing erythromycin stearate levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases eplerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases erlotinib levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 35. Erythromycin stearate decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases estradiol levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 36. Erythromycin stearate decreases conjugated synthetic estrogens levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases their levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 37. Erythromycin stearate decreases esterified estrogens levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases their levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 38. Erythromycin stearate decreases estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. It also increases estropipate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases eszopiclone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day. 40. Erythromycin stearate decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 41. Erythromycin stearate increases etoposide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 42. Erythromycin stearate increases eucalyptus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Erythromycin stearate increases exemestane levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Both erythromycin stearate and ezogabine prolong the QTc interval. Monitor the QT interval when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 45. Fedratinib increases erythromycin stearate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases finasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases finerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Both erythromycin stearate and flecainide prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases fludrocortisone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 50. Both erythromycin stearate and fluoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases fluvastatin toxicity. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 52. Both erythromycin stearate and fluvoxamine prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 53. Both erythromycin stearate and foscarnet prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 54. Fostamatinib increases erythromycin stearate levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrate drugs that may require dosage reduction. 55. Fostemsavir increases erythromycin stearate levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Monitor closely, especially at higher-than-recommended doses. 56. Both erythromycin stearate and gadobenate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 57. Both erythromycin stearate and gemtuzumab prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases gentamicin levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 59. Erythromycin stearate increases gepirone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 60. Goserelin increases erythromycin stearate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor. ...
